awd_titl_txt: Conference: Accelerating Translational Research through Increased Efficiency and Innovation in Development of Scientific Research
awd_abstract_narration:
This award supports the convening of a workshop and extended mentoring opportunities and collaborations in the area of scientific proposal development.  The workshop enhances rigor in research design, scientific discovery, and scientific writing for the public with the goal of increasing opportunities for innovation for early-career scientists nationwide. Broader impacts of the research include enhancing scientific proposal writing curricula at institutions across the nation and contributing to supporting early career scientists in developing project ideas and project proposals in key areas of social and behavioral science. It specifically supports the development of novel project ideas with translational impact in all of NSF’s scientific priority areas. The workshop and related mentoring activities expand the development of an innovative social scientific workforce for a variety of sectors in the nation’s economy.

The workshop involves participants from a wide range of scientific disciplines to enhance opportunities for multidisciplinary collaborative exchange and to generate and share best practices in scientific discovery and pluralistic engagement in science.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
This project brought together 37 experts in the social and life sciences through a series of virtual workshops to identify best practices in grant and research proposal development and to create new resources to support innovative, rigorous, and globally competitive research. The project addressed a longstanding challenge in research training: many students and early-career scholars receive limited formal instruction in how to develop successful grant proposals, despite the central role that external funding plays in advancing scientific discovery and professional careers.

The workshops focused on understanding how successful proposals are built through connections among ideas, researchers, institutions, communities, and broader societal impacts. Participants shared expertise, identified common obstacles in proposal development, and collaboratively developed strategies for strengthening grant writing instruction. The workshops also fostered collaboration among contributors from different institutions and areas of expertise. Evaluation results indicated that participants gained greater clarity about the goals and vision of the project, developed a stronger understanding of proposal development and revision processes, and built new professional connections that will support future collaborations.

A major outcome of the project was the completion of a comprehensive grant writing guide for social scientists. The manuscript will be published by Bloomsbury in the summer of 2027 and includes 31 chapters written by 34 experts and 49 practical exercises designed to help students and researchers develop proposal writing skills. The volume is intended for advanced undergraduate students, graduate students, postdoctoral scholars, junior faculty, and other researchers seeking to improve their ability to secure research funding. The guide emphasizes practical skill development, creativity, interdisciplinary thinking, and effective communication, providing accessible training resources that can be used across a wide range of institutions.

The project contributed to workforce development by providing a graduate research assistant with structured mentoring and hands-on experience in workshop organization, editorial processes, collaborative scholarship, and research management. These activities supported professional development and preparation for future careers in and beyond research and higher education.

The broader impacts of the project stem from its potential to improve grant-writing education and expand access to proposal development resources. By helping emerging scholars develop stronger funding proposals, the project contributes to strengthening research capacity, increasing participation in the scientific enterprise, and supporting the development of a more competitive and innovative research workforce. The resulting grant writing guide will make expert knowledge about proposal development more widely available and help researchers transform promising ideas into funded scientific projects.
